name: PA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+19 partisan lean in a Philadelphia-based district
Incumbent Brendan Boyle running with $5.6M cash on hand and no outside opposition
Republican challenger Jessica Arriaga has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Boyle holds a massive financial and incumbency advantage in a district that leans Democratic by 19 points, while Arriaga shows no measurable campaign infrastructure. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or Boyle's underfunded challenger gaining outside spending could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 2nd District, anchored in Philadelphia, leans Democratic by 19 points. Incumbent Brendan Boyle is seeking another term with more than $5.5 million on hand and no outside groups opposing him. His Republican challenger, Jessica Arriaga, has no reported fundraising or cash on hand, and no outside spending has appeared on her behalf.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Boyle's chances at roughly 97 percent. With the incumbent renominated and the challenger lacking visible resources, the seat is expected to remain safely Democratic.
